module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-configurable UART that stores control settings, transfers transmit data through a TX FIFO and serializer to uart_txd_o, samples uart_rxd_i into received bytes through an RX FIFO, generates interrupt and hardware-flow-control outputs, and returns control/status/data on its bus response. In simulation-enabled builds it can also emit written transmit bytes to a log process.

use-case flows.value: control-register settings for enable, simulation mode, hardware flow control, prescaler, baud divisor, interrupt enables, and FIFO clear commands
a transmit-data write request that enqueues one byte for transmission
queued transmit data loaded into the transmitter shift register and shifted out on uart_txd_o
serial input sampled from uart_rxd_i, assembled into a received byte, and handed to the RX FIFO input
interrupt requests and RX overrun status
stored control/status bits and received data returned on bus reads
receive-throttle decision exported on uart_rtsn_o when hardware flow control is enabled
control fields, engine state, flags, and outputs forced to known values on rstn_i='0', with FIFO clear decisions also asserted by disable/simulation/clear conditions

conceptual assets.reasoning: The control write path stores `ctrl.enable` at line 179, and later logic uses that stored bit to drive `clkgen_en_o` (line 228), qualify IRQ generation (lines 270 and 315), inject the enable into TX/RX engine state (lines 344 and 417), clear FIFOs when disabled (lines 259 and 304), clear overrun state (line 458), and force receive throttling when disabled (lines 473-475). Integrity is therefore established because enable/disable behavior across these flows must follow the stored setting; availability of normal TX/RX operation is conditional on this bit being `1` and the clear conditions being inactive. The write source is the excluded transport port `bus_req_i`, so the eligible references are the stored field and the exported enable.

The module stores `ctrl.prsc` and `ctrl.baud` on control writes at lines 182-183. `ctrl.prsc` selects `uart_clk` at line 229, and `ctrl.baud` is loaded into the TX and RX baud counters at lines 349, 368, 422, and 432; TX/RX bit movement advances only under `uart_clk` and counter-expiry conditions at lines 366-372 and 430-436. Corrupting these stored settings would mis-time transmit and receive operation, establishing Integrity; availability of serial progress depends on these settings producing the expected tick and reload values.

`ctrl.hwfc_en` is written at line 181, then used to qualify the transmitter's wait-for-send-permit condition at lines 358-360 and to decide whether `uart_rtsn_o` follows receive-side throttling or is forced low at lines 472-480. Integrity is established because handshake behavior in both transmit and receive-side flow-control paths must match this stored setting.

The control bits `ctrl.irq_tx_empty` and `ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf` are stored at lines 188-189 and are consumed by the TX IRQ generator at lines 270-272. Integrity is established because the configured TX FIFO conditions that are allowed to raise an interrupt must match these stored settings; availability of a TX interrupt request is conditional on `ctrl.enable` and the selected FIFO-status condition.

The control bits `ctrl.irq_rx_nempty`, `ctrl.irq_rx_half`, and `ctrl.irq_rx_full` are stored at lines 185-187 and are consumed by the RX IRQ generator at lines 315-318. Integrity is established because the configured RX FIFO conditions that are allowed to raise an interrupt must match these stored settings; availability of an RX interrupt request is conditional on `ctrl.enable` and the selected FIFO-status condition.

When the transmitter is idle, it loads `tx_engine.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata & '0'` at line 351 and enters the transmit path when data is available (lines 352-353). In the send state, it drives `tx_engine.txd <= tx_engine.sreg(0)` and shifts the register at lines 365-370, then exports the result at `uart_txd_o <= tx_engine.txd` on line 392. Integrity is established because the boundary output must match this load/shift/output chain; availability is conditional on enable, queued TX data, `uart_clk`, and baud countdown. The bus write source and FIFO carrier fields are excluded transport/sub-unit wiring, so the shift register and output port are the eligible references.

The receiver samples `uart_rxd_i` into `rx_engine.sync` at lines 408-410, detects the start transition at lines 424-425, and shifts sampled bits into `rx_engine.sreg` at line 434 under the `uart_clk`/baud-counter conditions of lines 430-436 until completion at lines 439-440. The low byte is then presented to the RX FIFO input at line 305 and later to readout at line 217. Integrity is established because the captured byte must follow this sampling and shift relation; availability is conditional on enable, the start transition, `uart_clk`, and baud countdown. The bus response and FIFO carrier fields are excluded, so the serial input port and receive shift register are the eligible references.

`rx_engine.over` is reset low at line 456, cleared again when the module is disabled at line 459, and set high when a received byte write occurs while the RX FIFO is not free at lines 460-461. The flag is reported on bus readout at line 214. Integrity is established because the reported overrun status must reflect exactly those overflow conditions; availability of the indication holds while enabled until cleared.

`irq_tx_o` is updated at lines 270-272 from `ctrl.enable` together with the configured TX interrupt bits and TX FIFO status conditions. This is a computed report decision delivered across a module boundary, so boundary-visible Integrity is established; availability is conditional on `ctrl.enable` and the selected TX FIFO condition becoming true.

`irq_rx_o` is updated at lines 315-318 from `ctrl.enable` together with the configured RX interrupt bits and RX FIFO status conditions. This is a computed report decision delivered across a module boundary, so boundary-visible Integrity is established; availability is conditional on `ctrl.enable` and the selected RX FIFO condition becoming true.

At lines 472-480, when hardware flow control is enabled the module drives `uart_rtsn_o` high if the UART is disabled or the RX FIFO is half full, and otherwise drives it low; when hardware flow control is disabled it drives low. This is a computed flow-control decision exported to another boundary consumer, so Integrity is established, and availability is conditional on the hardware-flow-control setting and the evaluated receive-side status.
